title: Metaprogramming Trade-offs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Metaprogramming Trade-offs”?
options: It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations. questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Metaprogramming Trade-offs”?
options: Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Metaprogramming Trade-offs”?
options: Metaprogramming Trade-offs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
questions.answer_key: Metaprogramming Trade-offs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Metaprogramming Trade-offs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
